meta.title: Blockbuster Could Have Bought Netflix For $50 Million. They Laughed Them Out Of The Room.
meta.hook: In 2000, Netflix walked into Blockbuster and offered to sell the entire company for fifty million dollars.
meta.description: In 2000, Netflix co-founders Reed Hastings and Marc Randolph pitched Blockbuster on buying their struggling DVD-by-mail startup for $50 million. Blockbuster's leadership passed. Within a decade Blockbuster was bankrupt, and Netflix went on to become one of the most valuable media companies in the world. (Blockbuster's then-CEO has since disputed how serious the meeting was — this is the widely reported version from Netflix's own founders.)

scenes.narration: In two thousand, Netflix walked into Blockbuster and offered to sell the entire company for fifty million dollars.

visual.visual_intent: A video rental store aisle with VHS and DVD cases, warm fluorescent light, archival documentary feel
visual.decision_reason: hook beat: the world Blockbuster was defending, hard cut

scenes.narration: Blockbuster's executives reportedly laughed them out of the room.

visual.visual_intent: Executives around a boardroom table, one leaning back dismissively, cool corporate light
visual.decision_reason: widely reported by Netflix co-founders; marked as reported, not confirmed by Blockbuster

scenes.narration: They saw a niche mail-order DVD service. Not a threat to a chain with thousands of stores nationwide.

visual.visual_intent: A DVD mailer envelope being pulled from a mailbox, warm suburban light, close and personal
visual.decision_reason: visualizes what Netflix actually was at the time

scenes.narration: Netflix kept building. In two thousand seven, it launched streaming, first as a small add-on to slow down cancellations.

visual.visual_intent: A person streaming video on a laptop from a couch at night, blue screen glow, cinematic

scenes.narration: That small add-on eventually replaced the entire disc business it started from.

visual.visual_intent: Nearly empty DVD store shelves under harsh light, a sense of decline, documentary realism

scenes.narration: Blockbuster filed for bankruptcy in twenty ten. Netflix is now worth more than most banks in America. Follow for more.

visual.visual_intent: A closed storefront with a faded sign, empty parking lot, late afternoon light, documentary tone
